aprilBoundaryNote: Two years are in play and both are right in their own frame. DfE states the National Minimum Allowance on a TAX year — GOV.UK heads the table 'Weekly allowances for the tax year from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027'. Councils apply their uplifts from 1 April: North Tyneside's decision record of 21 March 2025 says 'all uplifts in Allowances will take effect from 1 April 2025', and Rotherham's of 26 March 2024 says changes are 'implemented from or back dated to 1st April 2024'. effectiveFrom and effectiveTo follow the COUNCIL convention, because that is what decides what a carer is actually paid. For 1-5 April the two disagree, and the calculator says so on screen rather than picking a side. Backdating must segment on both dates once it is unblocked.

wales.verifyNote: Still not read from the 2026/27 circular itself, but materially stronger than it was. The Welsh Government circular of 26 February 2024 was supplied on 1 September 2026 and gives 2024/25 as a primary source. Walking those figures forward through the announced uplifts of 2.6% and 2.2% reproduces all three cells of this table exactly: 218 to 224 to 229, 199 to 204 to 208, and 248 to 254 to 260. Note the third chain settles a disagreement: a secondary report gave 2025/26 as 255 for the top band, which would produce 261 here rather than the 260 we serve. The primary source supports what we serve. Keep chasing the 2026/27 circular anyway.

anomalyCorroboration.source: Welsh Government circular of 26 February 2024, signed Alistair Davey
anomalyCorroboration.finding: Primary source. Prints 218 pounds for ages 0 to 4 against 199 pounds for 5 to 15, so the inversion is how the Welsh Government publishes the rates and not an error in a secondary report. The letter itself is linked rather than the Welsh Government home page, matching the 2024/25 entry.

anomalyCorroboration.source: Fostering news, '2025 Allowance Uplifts Across the UK'
anomalyCorroboration.finding: Records the 2025/26 Welsh NMA as £224 (0-4), £204 (5-10 and 11-15), £255 (16-17), the same inversion, in an independent year.

anomalyCorroboration.source: The Fostering Network, Foster Care Allowances
anomalyCorroboration.finding: Confirms the Welsh Government announced a 2.2% uplift for 2026/27. Applying 2.2% to the 2025/26 figures reproduces this table to the pound: 224 -> 228.9 (£229), 204 -> 208.5 (£208), 255 -> 260.6 (£260).

wales.userFacingNote: In Wales the rate for a child under 5 is higher than for a child aged 5 to 15. That is not a mistake on this site. It is how the Welsh Government publishes them.
wales.bandNote: The Welsh letter prints the top band as "16+", so it is marked openEnded here. The maxAge of 17 is this calculator's own cap, because the product is for children under 18 and the bands must tile 0 to 17 exactly. Not a transcription error, and not a closed band in the source. The letter also states the rates apply from 1 April, so Wales follows the council convention rather than the DfE tax year.
wales.note: The figures come from The Fostering Network's reproduced table, which is secondary, and verify stays true because of it. The Welsh Government letter carrying the 2026/27 rates has not been located after three searches. wg-nma-2026-27-approval is a separate primary record that the Minister approved the allowance; it carries no rate table, so it confirms the allowance exists and is not the source of these numbers. The two were previously conflated in one citation, which attributed the figures to a page that does not state them.

northern-ireland.note: NI pays kinship and non-kinship foster carers the same rate.

scotland.note: Scottish Recommended Allowance. A FLOOR with explicit foster/kinship parity. Councils may pay more. Not means tested in the SGO sense. CPI-uprated annually from March 2026.
